findings.location: pc-s54-twenty-eighth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a-homily.pdf, physical page 3 running head; source sections/homily/90-note.tex (no \runninghead after the properhomily environment)
findings.problem: The terminal Note on Sources and Delivery on page 3 sits under the running head 'Homily', which the properhomily environment set for the spoken pages. A reader skimming the furniture is told that the apparatus page is still part of the speech, although the page is full-width and titled differently. The sibling postconciliar homilies pc-s51 and pc-s52 share this pattern, and the content itself is correctly separated.
findings.required_result: If acted on, sections/homily/90-note.tex should set an interior running head with the shared \runninghead{...} command (for example 'Note on Sources and Delivery'), immediately after its \section* heading. Page 3's head would then name the apparatus. The homily's page count, two-column speech, and final-page colophon placement must not change.

observations.note: Two classes of furniture issue recur across postconciliar three-document productions and are caught only by cold visual review: a colophon near the paper edge on a full final page (VIS-001 here, previously also seen on the installed pc-s51 study) and a stale 'Homily' running head on the homily's terminal note (VIS-003). A mechanical gate on the colophon's lowest y position, and a shared default running head for the homily apparatus, would retire both.

summary: Independent full-page visual review of the three sealed artifacts of liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s54-twenty-eighth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a (provider claude). I recomputed every receipt hash and each matches REVIEW_INPUTS and research/artifacts.json. I viewed the build-artifacts-0001 contact sheets (study sheets 001-002, concise 001, homily 001), then rasterised every page afresh from the sealed bytes at 100 dpi and opened each page full-size. Reviewed artifacts and page coverage: (1) build/claude/.../pc-s54-twenty-eighth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a.pdf, sha256 9adfbff33dfed4bf59e457a38d5e97190038d266d877f80cc3835d6fa5b5ba3a, 38 physical pages, pages 1-38 all inspected; (2) build/claude/.../pc-s54-twenty-eighth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a-synthesis.pdf, sha256 b748378f675185c8c32bc8e16b4632ecfc64a7663dc87a225b91e6c1e4b3b35a, 12 physical pages, pages 1-12 all inspected; (3) build/claude/.../pc-s54-twenty-eighth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a-homily.pdf, sha256 857e4db160006c23638eb94f8b25c3a2354c7300b38a5f9fee4e70904a9e0af2, 4 physical pages, pages 1-4 all inspected. Pagination evidence: synthesis.aux 9fa9be30e38d95a8a5982b2975b0f1b92be0a200bb5d6e0504fb47b87b362622 and study .aux 3b0b26253a1351c077db812be32adfbcfdff755e6379e95ad709f3b96429c352, both matching the seal. All fonts in all three PDFs are embedded Latin Modern Type 1 subsets. The pages are US Letter, with 0.75 in margins (text x 52-560 pt) and 11-pt article body type. They are monochrome and contain no raster images. The settled build logs show no overfull boxes, undefined references or rerun requests. The study (38 pages, within 20-50) has no columns and a consistent section, subsection, \properlane and fourSenses hierarchy across its three interpretations. Its tables (the elements at a glance, the comparison, the chronology dossier and the branches) break cleanly with repeated header rows. Its deliberate breaks on pages 28 and 31 fall at the start of a four-senses block and of the dossier, and the final page carries References, Last revised and the complete colophon, ending at y 571.7 pt. The concise study (12 pages, within 10-12) has no columns, and its opening matches the settled zref evidence on the actual pages. Page 1 holds the complete 14-row map in liturgical order, with options marked, and exactly four sense rows. Page 2 holds Scriptural Date and Location alone, complete and readable. Pages 3-4 carry a substantive Themes and Movement argument. Developed commentary begins on page 5 and visibly interleaves the alternatives on pages 5-10. The standing VIS-001 defect from iteration 0 is cleared: the four-line colophon, including the LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY.md pointer, now ends at y 744.8 pt on page 12, the same page as the References and timestamp. That is above the ordinary footer baseline (about 764 pt) and 47 pt from the paper edge. The repair was made by shortening four References entries, with no change to type size or geometry and no rights-only page. The iteration-0 advisory VIS-002 is also cleared: the descriptive line now stands upright and capitalised in the subtitle field. The homily has a full-width title and subtitle, a two-column speech on pages 1-2 with comfortable, recoverable paragraphs and no inline apparatus, and then a separate full-width Note on Sources and Delivery and References on pages 3-4, ending with the colophon at y 646.8 pt. As designed, the shared colophon macro suppresses the folio and running head on each final page. Limits: the inspection was at 100 dpi full pages plus PDF text-geometry measurement, with no physical print test. This is not a formatting migration, so no text-preservation comparison was owed. Verdict: PASS, with one advisory.
